name: n18-sizing
title: Sizing a 3-stage fabric
spec: Left: formulas for R-port switches at 1:1: 'spines = R/2', 'max leaves = R', 'max servers = R x R/2 = R^2/2'. Right: worked example with 64-port 400G switches: each leaf 32 downlinks + 32 uplinks, 32 spines, up to 64 leaves, up to 2,048 endpoint ports = 256 servers with eight GPUs each. Small leaf-spine drawing with a leaf split into 'half down to servers / half up to spines'. Orange note: 'beyond R^2/2 endpoints, build pods: 5-stage reaches R^3/4 (65,536 for R = 64)'.
cap: With R-port switches a 1:1 three-stage fabric reaches R squared over two endpoints.

name: n18-fivestage
title: Scaling table: 3-stage to 5-stage
spec: Table with columns Config, GPUs, Leaves, Spines, Super-spines, Oversubscription. Rows: 1 row (one rail group) 256 / 8 / 4 / none / 1:1; 2 rows 512 / 16 / 8 / none / 1:1; 8 rows (3-stage, 64-port) 2,048 / 64 / 32 / none / 1:1; 5-stage 1K-GPU blocks 2,048 / 64 / 64 / 32 / 1:1; 5-stage 4 blocks 4,096 / 128 / 128 / 32 / 2:1 at super-spine; 5-stage 8 blocks 8,192 / 256 / 256 / 32 / 4:1 at super-spine (orange). Divider line between the 3-stage rows and 5-stage rows labelled 'add pods and super-spines'.
cap: Growing beyond one three-stage build needs super-spines or oversubscription of the upper tier.

name: n18-oversub
title: Oversubscription ratios
spec: Leaf switch drawn with server-facing ports below and uplinks above, two worked cases. Case 1: d downlinks and u uplinks gives ratio d:u; 48 downlinks and 16 uplinks = 3:1. Case 2: ToR with 320 Gb/s of server ports and 180 Gb/s of uplinks = 1.78:1. Definition line: 'oversubscription = bandwidth offered to endpoints over bandwidth into the fabric (worst-case contention)'. Orange note: 'Non-blocking and non-contending are different; packet-switched fabrics cannot be truly non-blocking because of incast'.
cap: Oversubscription is the ratio of server bandwidth to uplink bandwidth at a tier.

name: n18-failure
title: Capacity left after a spine fails
spec: Bar comparison. Formula in monospace: 'capacity kept = (S-1)/S of uplink capacity'. Two bars: S = 32 spines, one down: 96.9% (green, almost full); S = 4 spines, one down: 75% (orange). Small leaf with its uplinks, one greyed out. Footer: 'A 1:1 design stays oversubscribed until the failure is repaired' and bar 'Work out what survives losing one spine, one leaf and one rail group'.
cap: The fewer spines a fabric has, the bigger the capacity loss when one spine fails.
